verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior and of the Lord Jesus Christ, our hope,
verses.1:2: to Timothy, a genuine child in faith: Grace, mercy, peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.1:3: Just as I urged you to remain in Ephesus while I was going to Macedonia, so that you might charge certain people not to teach a different doctrine,
verses.1:4: nor to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which produce speculations rather than the stewardship of God that is in faith—
verses.1:5: Now the goal of this charge is love from a pure heart and a good conscience and a sincere faith,
verses.1:6: from which some, missing the mark, turned aside into empty talk,
verses.1:7: wanting to be teachers of the law, yet understanding neither what they are saying nor the matters about which they make confident assertions.
verses.1:8: Now we know that the law is good, if one uses it lawfully,
verses.1:9: knowing this, that law is not laid down for a righteous person, but for the lawless and rebellious, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for those who kill their fathers and those who kill their mothers, for murderers,
verses.1:10: for the sexually immoral, for men who lie with men, for slave traders, for liars, for perjurers, and for anything else that stands contrary to sound teaching,
verses.1:11: in accordance with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I was entrusted.
verses.1:12: I give thanks to the One who strengthened me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because He considered me faithful, appointing me to service,
verses.1:13: even though previously I was a blasphemer and a persecutor and a violent aggressor; yet I was shown mercy because I acted ignorantly in unbelief,
verses.1:14: and the grace of our Lord overflowed exceedingly, along with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
verses.1:15: Trustworthy is this saying and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners—of whom I am the first.
verses.1:16: Yet for this reason I was shown mercy, so that in me as the first, Jesus Christ might display complete patience as a pattern for those who were going to believe in Him for eternal life.
verses.1:17: Now to the King of the ages—incorruptible, invisible, the only God—be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.1:18: This charge I entrust to you, child Timothy, in accordance with the prophecies previously spoken about you, so that through them you may wage the good warfare,
verses.1:19: holding onto faith and a good conscience, which some have pushed away and have suffered shipwreck regarding the faith.
verses.1:20: Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan so that they might be disciplined not to blaspheme.
verses.2:1: Therefore I urge, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be offered on behalf of all people,
verses.2:2: for kings and for all those who are in high authority, so that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity.
verses.2:3: This is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior,
verses.2:4: who desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
verses.2:5: For there is one God, and one mediator as well between God and human beings, the man Christ Jesus,
verses.2:6: who gave Himself as a ransom on behalf of all, the testimony at its proper times.
verses.2:7: For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle—I am speaking the truth in Christ, I am not lying—a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
verses.2:8: Therefore I want the men in every place to pray, lifting up holy hands without anger and disputing.
verses.2:9: Likewise, that women adorn themselves in respectable attire, with modesty and self-control, not with braided hair and gold, or pearls, or costly clothing,
verses.2:10: but with what is proper for women professing reverence for God, through good works.
verses.2:11: Let a woman learn in quietness, in full submission.
verses.2:12: And I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man, but to be in quietness.
verses.2:13: For Adam was formed first, then Eve;
verses.2:14: and Adam was not deceived, but the woman, having been thoroughly deceived, fell into transgression.
verses.2:15: Yet she will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and sanctification with self-control.
verses.3:1: Trustworthy is this saying: if anyone aspires to oversight, he desires a good work.
verses.3:2: Therefore the overseer must be above reproach, a husband of one wife, sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach,
verses.3:3: not given to wine, not violent, but gentle, not quarrelsome, free from the love of money,
verses.3:4: managing his own household well, having children in submission with all dignity;
verses.3:5: (but if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he care for the church of God?)
verses.3:6: not a new convert, so that he may not become puffed up with pride and fall into the condemnation of the devil.
verses.3:7: Moreover, he must also have a good testimony from those outside, so that he may not fall into disgrace and the snare of the devil.
verses.3:8: Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued, not devoted to much wine, not greedy for dishonest gain,
verses.3:9: holding the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience.
verses.3:10: And let these also be tested first; then let them serve as deacons, being blameless.
verses.3:11: Women likewise must be dignified, not slanderers, sober-minded, faithful in all things.
verses.3:12: Let deacons be husbands of one wife, managing their children and their own households well.
verses.3:13: For those who have served well as deacons gain for themselves a good standing and great boldness in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:14: I am writing these things to you, hoping to come to you soon;
verses.3:15: but if I am delayed, so that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the household of God, which is the church of the living God, a pillar and foundation of the truth.
verses.3:16: And undeniably great is the mystery of godliness: He who was revealed in the flesh, was vindicated in the Spirit, appeared to angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed on in the world, was taken up in glory.
verses.4:1: Yet the Spirit expressly says that in later times some will depart from the faith, paying heed to misleading spirits and teachings of demons,
verses.4:2: through the hypocrisy of liars, who have been seared in their own conscience,
verses.4:3: who forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods that God created to be partaken of with thanksgiving by those who believe and have come to know the truth.
verses.4:4: For every created thing of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving,
verses.4:5: for it is sanctified through God's word and prayer.
verses.4:6: By setting these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, being nourished on the words of the faith and of the good teaching that you have closely followed.
verses.4:7: But refuse profane and old wives' myths. Instead, train yourself for godliness;
verses.4:8: for bodily training is beneficial for a little, while godliness is beneficial for all things, holding the promise of the present life and of the life to come.
verses.4:9: Trustworthy is the saying and worthy of all acceptance.
verses.4:10: For toward this goal we labor and strive, because we have fixed our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of believers.
verses.4:12: Let no one think lightly of your youth, but become an example to the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
verses.4:13: Until I come, give attention to the reading, to exhortation, to teaching.
verses.4:14: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the council of elders.
verses.4:15: Practice these things; be absorbed in them, so that your progress may be evident to all.
verses.4:16: Pay close attention to yourself and to the teaching; persevere in these things, for by doing this you will save both yourself and those who listen to you.
verses.5:1: Do not sharply rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as a father, to younger men as brothers,
verses.5:2: to older women as mothers, to younger women as sisters, in all purity.
verses.5:3: Honor widows who are truly widows.
verses.5:4: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to practice godliness toward their own household and to make repayment to their parents, for this is acceptable before God.
verses.5:5: Now she who is truly a widow and has been left alone has fixed her hope on God and continues in petitions and prayers night and day,
verses.5:6: whereas she who lives in self-indulgence is dead even while she lives.
verses.5:7: Command these things as well, so that they may be above reproach.
verses.5:8: Yet if anyone does not care for his own, and especially for members of his household, he has renounced the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
verses.5:9: Let a widow be enrolled if she is not less than sixty years old, the wife of one husband,
verses.5:10: well attested for good works: if she has raised children, if she has shown hospitality, if she has washed the saints' feet, if she has assisted the afflicted, if she has devoted herself to every good work.
verses.5:11: But refuse younger widows; for whenever their passions draw them away from Christ, they want to marry,
verses.5:12: thus incurring judgment because they have set aside their first faith.
verses.5:13: At the same time they also learn to be idle, going around from house to house; and not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, talking about things they ought not to.
verses.5:14: Therefore I desire younger women to marry, to bear children, to manage their households, and to give the adversary no opportunity for slander;
verses.5:15: for some have already turned aside after Satan.
verses.5:16: If any believing woman has widows, let her assist them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it may assist those who are truly widows.
verses.5:17: Let the elders who lead well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in word and teaching.
verses.5:18: For the Scripture says, "You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing," and, "The worker is worthy of his wages."
verses.5:19: Do not accept an accusation against an elder except on the basis of two or three witnesses.
verses.5:20: Rebuke those who persist in sin before all, so that the rest may also have fear.
verses.5:21: I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels to keep these things without prejudgment, doing nothing out of partiality.
verses.5:22: Do not lay hands hastily on anyone, nor share in the sins of others; keep yourself pure.
verses.5:23: No longer drink only water, but use a little wine on account of your stomach and your frequent ailments.
verses.5:24: The sins of some people are conspicuous, going ahead to judgment, while for others they follow behind as well;
verses.5:25: likewise, good works are also conspicuous, and those that are otherwise cannot be hidden.
verses.6:1: Let all who are slaves under a yoke regard their own masters as worthy of all honor, so that the name of God and the teaching may not be maligned.
verses.6:2: And those who have believing masters must not look down on them because they are brothers; rather, let them serve all the more, because those who partake of the benefit are believers and beloved. Teach and exhort these things.
verses.6:3: If anyone teaches a different doctrine and does not consent to sound words—those of our Lord Jesus Christ—and to the teaching that accords with godliness,
verses.6:4: he is puffed up with conceit, understanding nothing, yet having an unhealthy craving for controversies and battles over words, out of which arise envy, strife, slanders, wicked suspicions,
verses.6:5: and constant friction among people corrupted in mind and deprived of the truth, who suppose that godliness is a source of gain.
verses.6:6: Yet godliness with contentment is a great source of gain.
verses.6:7: For we have brought nothing into the world, so that we cannot carry anything out either;
verses.6:8: and having food and covering, with these we will be content.
verses.6:9: But those who desire to become rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many senseless and harmful desires that plunge people into ruin and destruction.
verses.6:10: For the love of money is a root of all evils; by craving it, some have strayed away from the faith and pierced themselves through with many pangs.
verses.6:11: But as for you, O man of God, flee from these things; pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, and gentleness.
verses.6:12: Contend in the good contest of the faith; take hold of eternal life, to which you were called, and you made the good confession before many witnesses.
verses.6:13: I command you before God, who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus, who bore witness to the good confession before Pontius Pilate,
verses.6:14: that you keep the commandment spotless and above reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.6:15: which He will display at the proper times—the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule,
verses.6:16: who alone possesses immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no human being has seen nor can see. To Him be honor and eternal dominion. Amen.
verses.6:17: Command those who are rich in the present age not to be arrogant nor to fix their hope on the uncertainty of wealth, but on God, who richly provides us with all things for enjoyment;
verses.6:18: to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous, ready to share,
verses.6:19: storing up for themselves a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of what is truly life.
verses.6:20: O Timothy, guard the deposit, turning away from profane empty chatter and the opposing arguments of what is falsely called knowledge,
verses.6:21: which some have professed and so missed the mark regarding the faith. Grace be with you.

notes.1:1: Textual note: the Saints Greek Critical Text reads "the Lord Jesus Christ" (Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ) rather than "Christ Jesus" alone.
notes.1:4: Verses 3–4 form an incomplete sentence (anacoluthon) in Greek, breaking off before a main clause. The noun οἰκονομίαν ("stewardship") can also denote God's household administration or saving plan.
notes.1:10: The rare compound ἀρσενοκοίταις (literally "men who lie with males") echoes the Greek wording of Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13 in the Septuagint.
notes.1:16: "First" (πρώτῳ) echoes v. 15 and can signify either foremost in degree ("worst") or first in a prototypical line of recipients of Christ's mercy.
notes.2:7: Textual note: the Saints Greek Critical Text includes "in Christ" (ἐν Χριστῷ), which is omitted in several early manuscripts.
notes.2:12: The verb αὐθεντεῖν occurs only here in the New Testament; its exact nuance is debated, ranging from "exercise authority over" to "domineer over."
notes.2:15: "Saved through childbearing" (διὰ τῆς τεκνογονίας) is variously understood as spiritual perseverance in family faithfulness, physical preservation in childbirth, or salvation through the birth of the Messiah; note also the Greek shift from singular ("she") to plural ("they").
notes.3:2: Literally "a man of one woman" (μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἄνδρα), commonly understood as requiring marital fidelity; the same phrase appears for deacons in v. 12.
notes.3:11: The Greek noun γυναῖκας ("women") lacks a possessive pronoun here and is debated as referring either to female deacons (deaconesses) or to the wives of deacons.
notes.3:16: Textual note: the Saints Greek Critical Text reads the relative pronoun "He who" (Ὃς), whereas later manuscripts read "God" (θεός). The six parallel clauses are widely recognized as an early Christian hymn or confession.
notes.4:2: "Seared" renders a Greek verb literally meaning "branded with a hot iron," denoting a conscience either cauterized into insensitivity or marked with a brand of ownership.
notes.4:3: Greek employs a single participle ("forbidding") over both "to marry" and "to abstain from foods," implying a contrasting verb such as "requiring" for the second clause.
notes.4:10: The critical text reads "we strive" (ἀγωνιζόμεθα), whereas some later manuscripts read "we suffer reproach" (ὀνειδιζόμεθα).
notes.4:13: "The reading" (τῇ ἀναγνώσει) most likely refers to the public reading of Scripture in the assembled church.
notes.5:4: "Parents" translates Greek προγόνοις ("forebears"), which in this context includes both living parents and grandparents.
notes.5:12: "First faith" (τὴν πρώτην πίστιν) here likely refers to an initial pledge or commitment of single-minded devotion to Christ.
notes.5:16: The critical text reads "any believing woman" (πιστή), while some later manuscripts expand the phrase to "any believing man or woman."
notes.5:18: The first quotation is from Deuteronomy 25:4, and the second matches Jesus' saying in Luke 10:7, both introduced under "the Scripture says."
notes.6:2: "Those who partake of the benefit" most likely refers to the believing masters who benefit from the faithful service of their Christian slaves.
notes.6:7: The critical text has the conjunction ὅτι ("so that" or "because") directly linking the clauses; some later manuscripts add "it is clear" (δῆλον) to smooth the syntax.
notes.6:10: Greek has no definite article before "root" (ῥίζα), so the phrase may be read as "a root" or "the root" of all evils.
notes.6:20: "The deposit" (τὴν παραθήκην) refers to the apostolic gospel and sound teaching entrusted to Timothy's care.
notes.6:21: The pronoun "you" (ὑμῶν) is plural in the critical text, extending the closing blessing beyond Timothy to the entire congregation.
